title: Scorer invocation timeout is enforced only inside Scorer.run, via a re-entrant daemon thread
answers: how does a custom scorer time out during mlflow.genai.evaluate
why does a hanging scorer stall the whole evaluation
why does my scorer run in a MlflowScorer thread
body:
Symptom: a custom scorer hangs (e.g. a wedged LLM judge call) and the whole evaluation or monitoring run stalls.
Root cause: a scorer is executed only through Scorer.run in mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py; without a bound on that call nothing limits one invocation.
Fix pattern: keep all timeout logic in Scorer.run. When a timeout is set, Scorer._run_with_timeout runs self.run in a daemon thread (name MlflowScorer-<name>) with the _in_scorer_timeout ContextVar set, so the nested run() skips the timeout branch. On overrun it raises MlflowTimeoutError, which the harness converts to a SCORER_ERROR feedback.
Constraints: the worker must still execute through a Scorer.run frame, because telemetry walks the stack to attribute a scorer's callsite. Do not replace this with signal.alarm, since scorers run in harness worker threads where SIGALRM is unavailable. Do not add a second timeout layer for ensemble or session scorers; they already funnel through run().
applies: Any change to Scorer.run, scorer execution, or the evaluation/monitoring harness that invokes scorers.
says: Evaluation job hangs indefinitely when a custom judge metric gets stuck.
Prevent hanging model evaluation metrics from stalling the entire evaluation run.
Evaluation monitoring gets blocked forever by an unresponsive custom evaluation scoring call.
Report an execution error when an automated scoring judge exceeds its time limit.
Model assessment run does not terminate after a third-party evaluation scorer times out.
search: Scorer invocation timeouts in mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py are enforced strictly inside Scorer.run using a re-entrant daemon thread. When configured, Scorer._run_with_timeout executes self.run on a MlflowScorer daemon thread with _in_scorer_timeout set, raising MlflowTimeoutError on overrun to produce SCORER_ERROR feedback. Execution must maintain a Scorer.run stack frame for telemetry, signal.alarm cannot be used due to worker threads lacking SIGALRM, and ensemble or session scorers must not add a second timeout layer.
